name: STAR Orbit — initial orbit determination from three positions (Gibbs, Herrick-Gibbs)
summary: Velocity at the middle of three position vectors by Gibbs' method (cancellation-free form) and Herrick-Gibbs, with the measured domain of each (crossover near 0.4 degrees), agreement with Orekit IodGibbs within 8e-9 and explicit refusal of non-coplanar, collinear or impossible geometry.
reference: Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, Example 7-3 (Gibbs): r1 = (0, 0, 6378.137), r2 = (0, -4464.696, -5102.509), r3 = (0, 5740.323, 3189.068) km -> v2 = (0, 5.531148, -5.191806) km/s
reference_observed: all three components within 2.2e-7 km/s of the printed values; Example 7-4 (Herrick-Gibbs) first two components within 1e-6 km/s, third component not asserted

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: km, km/s, s by default; any consistent set with the matching mu (tested in metres)
review.G-06: no external data; cross-check corpus generated with a fixed seed
review.G-08: pure functions, standard library only, no IO
review.G-13: ValueError for invalid input and for geometry that defines no orbit; no iteration
